ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A kind of waterbird has now been found to mainly inhabit the shallow water and mudflats of a certain lake area, and to take certain plants in the lake area as its main food source. Answer the following questions. The biological components such as the plants, waterbirds, and bacteria of the lake area and the inorganic environment constitute an ecosystem. The schematic diagram of energy flowing through this kind of waterbird on the food chain is as follows. ①, ②, and ③ indicate biological life activity processes. What are ①, ②, and ③ respectively?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: ①. The assimilation amount of the waterbird    ②. The energy dissipated as heat energy by the waterbird through respiration    ③. The energy flowing to decomposers

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A kind of waterbird has now been found to mainly inhabit the shallow water and mudflats of a certain lake area, and to take certain plants in the lake area as its main food source. Answer the following questions. The biological components such as the plants, waterbirds, and bacteria of the lake area and the inorganic environment constitute an ecosystem. The schematic diagram of energy flowing through this kind of waterbird on the food chain is as follows. ①, ②, and ③ indicate biological life activity processes. What are ①, ②, and ③ respectively?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: ①. The assimilation amount of the waterbird ②. The energy dissipated as heat energy by the waterbird through respiration ③. The energy flowing to decomposers
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the box on the left side of the figure is “waterbird ingestion,” with an arrow flowing to the middle box numbered ①; ① then flows to the right to “used for growth, development, and reproduction.” Above ① there is number ②, with an arrow pointing upward to “dissipation.” “Waterbird ingestion” also has an arrow going downward and then rightward, labeled “feces,” flowing to the box numbered ③; below “used for growth, development, and reproduction” there is an arrow labeled “remains, debris,” also flowing to ③. Then reason: in ecosystem energy flow, the energy ingested by animals minus the energy in feces is the assimilation amount absorbed by the animal and entering the body, so ① is the assimilation amount of the waterbird. Part of the assimilation amount is dissipated in the form of heat energy through respiration, corresponding to ② from ① upward to “dissipation” in the figure. Feces as well as remains and debris can all be decomposed and used by decomposers, so ③ indicates the energy flowing to decomposers.
